question: An item is marked at ₹150. A customer gets a 10% discount on it. If the seller still makes a profit of 25%, what is the cost price of the item?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of Cost Price (CP) to Marked Price (MP) can be directly calculated by the formula:

CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)

⇒ CP / 150 = (100 − 10) / (100 + 25)

⇒ CP / 150 = 90 / 125 = 18 / 25

⇒ CP = (18 / 25) × 150 = 18 × 6 = ₹108

**∴ The correct answer is ₹108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹150, Discount = 10%, Profit = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)
